summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after falling at home, resulting in a closed medial tibial plateau fracture. Due to multiple comorbidities including morbid obesity, chronic heart failure, and HIV, surgical intervention was deemed high-risk, so the fracture was managed conservatively with a hinged knee brace and strict non-weight-bearing status. She remained stable throughout the hospitalization, with no complications. An asymptomatic urinary tract infection was treated with ciprofloxacin. Her chronic conditions, including HIV, asthma, and heart failure, were maintained on existing regimens without change. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with instructions for continued brace use, pain management, and follow-up care.
